verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Senior Inter Maths-2A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.65 — SAQ chapter 11 Partial Fractions, answer 97 (the book's 'SPECIAL TYPE'). Printed appearances: AP 18. ⚠ THE 1+1+1+1 SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S — this chapter prints no [N Marks] tags against any answer, only tick boxes. The split is the four moves of the method (set up the form · clear the denominators · find the constants · write the result), one mark each, and the SAME split and the SAME step ids (s1_form, s2_identity, s3_constants, s4_result) are used on all fifteen cards of this unit, deliberately: they are one method over different fractions. For the improper fractions the division lives inside s1_form, and for the (x − 3)³ question the substitution x − 3 = y takes the place of the form. The book's SAQ chapter header carries ★★★ and reads '4 Marks'; that star is the CHAPTER's rank, not this question's. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Paper position: Maths-2A Section B runs Q11–Q17 at 4 marks each, answer any 5 of 7; Q15 is the Partial Fractions slot (the chapter has no Section A or Section C slot). Not asked at Q15 in any of the five model papers. No two-book check and no board back-test exist for this paper — recorded, not hidden. The book solves this by the substitution x − 3 = y and never writes the A/(x − 3) + B/(x − 3)² + C/(x − 3)³ form; the card follows the book route because it is shorter and exact, and says in s1 why the general form would also work. On this card the four step ids mean: s1_form = the substitution, s2_identity = expanding the numerator in y, s3_constants = splitting into three fractions, s4_result = writing back in x. Truth check: putting x = 4 (y = 1) gives (16 + 20 + 7)/1 = 43 on the left and 1 + 11 + 31 = 43 on the right.

recall_prompt: Say how you would resolve (x² + 5x + 7)/(x − 3)³ into partial fractions — name each move in order.
insider_note: One linear factor cubed means the substitution x − 3 = y does the whole question — expand, divide term by term, no constants to solve; the last mark is putting y = x − 3 back.

steps.label: Put x − 3 = y
steps.margin_note: First mark. The denominator is ONE linear factor cubed. Instead of the three-constant form, put x − 3 = y so the denominator becomes y³ and the numerator becomes a polynomial in y.
lines: Put x − 3 = y, so x = y + 3.

recall.must_convey: That the substitution x − 3 = y turns the fraction into ((y + 3)² + 5(y + 3) + 7)/y³.
accept: put x minus three equals y so x is y plus three and the fraction becomes y plus three squared plus five into y plus three plus seven all over y cubed
substitute y for x minus three so the denominator is y cubed
let y equal x minus 3 and rewrite the numerator in terms of y
x minus three ni y ani pettali, appudu x equals y plus three, denominator y cube avutundi
change the variable to y equals x minus three so the denominator is a single power

steps.why: When the whole denominator is one factor raised to a power, a substitution makes it a single power of y, and any polynomial over y³ splits into powers of 1/y by simple division. This avoids finding three constants by comparison.
common_mistakes: Writing x = y − 3 instead of x = y + 3.
Substituting in the denominator only and leaving the numerator in x.
Setting up A/(x − 3) + B/(x − 3)² + C/(x − 3)³ and then making errors in the coefficient comparison; it works, but the substitution is shorter.

steps.label: Expand the numerator
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Expand (y + 3)² = y² + 6y + 9 and 5(y + 3) = 5y + 15, then add the 7. Collect like terms carefully: the constants 9 + 15 + 7 = 31.

recall.must_convey: That the numerator expands to y² + 11y + 31.
accept: expand y plus three squared plus five into y plus three plus seven to get y squared plus eleven y plus thirty one
the numerator becomes y squared plus eleven y plus thirty one
y square plus 6y plus 9 plus 5y plus 15 plus 7 is y square plus 11y plus 31
numerator expand cheste y square plus eleven y plus thirty one vastundi
collect the terms to get y squared plus eleven y plus thirty one

steps.why: The split in the next step reads the coefficients 1, 11, 31 directly from this polynomial, so the expansion must be exact. Every constant in the final answer comes from this one line.
common_mistakes: Expanding (y + 3)² as y² + 9 and dropping the 6y.

steps.label: Split into three fractions
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Divide each term of the numerator by y³ separately. y²/y³ = 1/y, 11y/y³ = 11/y², 31/y³ stays. No constants to solve for.

recall.must_convey: That dividing each term by y³ gives 1/y + 11/y² + 31/y³.
accept: divide each term by y cubed to get one over y plus eleven over y squared plus thirty one over y cubed
y squared by y cubed is one by y, eleven y by y cubed is eleven by y squared and thirty one by y cubed stays
split it term by term into 1 by y plus 11 by y square plus 31 by y cube
prathi term ni y cube tho divide cheste one by y plus eleven by y square plus thirty one by y cube
separate the fraction into three fractions with powers of y in the denominators

steps.why: A sum over a single denominator is the sum of the separate fractions. Cancelling the powers of y in each one gives the partial fractions directly, which is why the substitution route needs no A, B, C.
common_mistakes: Cancelling y²/y³ to y instead of 1/y.
Writing 11/y instead of 11/y² for the middle term.
Leaving the answer as one fraction over y³; the question asks for it split.

steps.label: Write the result
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Put y = x − 3 back. The three denominators become (x − 3), (x − 3)², (x − 3)³. Write the original fraction on the left.

recall.must_convey: That replacing y by x − 3 gives 1/(x − 3) + 11/(x − 3)² + 31/(x − 3)³.
accept: put y equals x minus three back to get one over x minus three plus eleven over x minus three squared plus thirty one over x minus three cubed
replace y with x minus three in all three fractions
the answer is 1 by x minus 3 plus 11 by x minus 3 square plus 31 by x minus 3 cube

change back to x so the denominators are x minus three, x minus three squared and x minus three cubed

steps.why: The question was asked in x, so an answer left in y is not the answer. Putting the substitution back is the last move and it earns the final mark.
common_mistakes: Writing x + 3 instead of x − 3 when putting back.
Not checking: put x = 4, so y = 1. Left side (16 + 20 + 7)/1 = 43, right side 1 + 11 + 31 = 43. If the two sides differ, a coefficient is wrong.
